root.name: Dutch Defense: Manhattan Gambit, Anti-Classical Line

overview: White plays 2.Qd3 and meets the Dutch with 3.g4 whichever way Black replies. After 2...e6 3.g4 fxg4 Black has a pawn and White gets Qg3 and the open g-file, plus ideas around e5 and a quick Bg5. It is a trappy attacking idea that holds up poorly against calm play.

white_ideas.idea: Offer g4 and open the g-file
Bring the queen to g3 with Qg3 and Bg5
Attack the kingside with h3 and Nf3

black_ideas.idea: Take on g4 and return the pawn at a good moment
Challenge the queen and the centre with ...d5 or ...Nf6

typical_structures.structure: White queen on d3 with g-pawn thrown forward
Open g-file towards a castled king

character.notes: The Manhattan is a trappy gambit that can win quickly if Black errs.

gambit.notes: Black can take on g4 and keep the pawn with ...Nf6 and ...d5.

approach.notes: Rare among strong players; mainly a surprise.

level.notes: The attack is simple but it is a dubious line.

character.reason: White throws the g-pawn forward early so one error can lose fast.

gambit.reason: White offers the g4 pawn for attacking chances.

soundness.reason: The attack runs out of steam against sensible defence.

structure.reason: The g-file opens and the centre is fluid.

approach.reason: Strong players hardly ever choose it.

plans.reason: The g4 break aims at the kingside.
